newsitem.title: USA: Nike CFO sees FY98 profit growth of 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nike CFO sees FY98 profit growth of 15 pct.

text.p: Nike Inc Chief Financial Officer Robert Falcone said Tuesday he expected earnings for the current 1998 fiscal year to be about 15 percent higher than the $795.8 million reported for fiscal 1997.
Falcone said in a conference call with analysts and reporters that the company was on track to meet its long-term goal of increasing revenues by 15 to 18 percent a year.
But he said gross profit margins in the current year would decline by about 0.5 percentage point as the company builds its sales and marketing network outside the United States.

Nike President Tom Clarke said in the conference call he felt "very good" about the year ahead, despite advance orders that show U.S. footwear sales flattening in the company's fiscal second quarter, which begins September 1.
He noted that business remained strong in Nike's increasingly important overseas markets, where growth prospects are more promising.
Clarke also said he expected strong growth in the United States in the coming year in several important categories including golf, basketball and soccer.

A newly launched Jordan brand of footwear and apparel, sporting a logo of basketball star Michael Jordan and separate from the main Nike brand, should generate sales of $280 million to $300 million, Clarke said.
